intro: This site is about budget local AI across hardware and across Windows, Linux and macOS. The Builder checks PC parts (slots, lanes, power, cooling); this page covers what runs where. Support changes with every driver and release, so each statement says where it was read and when.

verified_by_us.claim: AMD's Windows HIP SDK 7.2.0 does not support the Radeon RX 6000 series (6600 to 6950 XT), the Radeon PRO W6800 or the Radeon PRO VII (MI50-class gfx906). It does support the RX 7000 and RX 9000 series, the R9700 and the Ryzen AI Max chips.

os.summary: Windows is easiest with NVIDIA (CUDA driver only, no toolkit needed for Ollama/LM Studio). AMD works two ways: ROCm/HIP only on RDNA3/RDNA4 Radeons (RX 7000/9000, W7000, Ryzen AI Max) and NOT on RX 6000/V620 per AMD's Windows table; everything else falls back to Vulkan, which Ollama and llama.cpp support. Intel Arc runs via llama.cpp SYCL (Windows 11) or Vulkan. Pascal/Volta datacenter cards work on the R580 driver but are a hassle on Windows (see pitfalls).
tools: Ollama for Windows (Windows 10 22H2+; NVIDIA driver 551.61+; AMD needs ROCm v7/HIP7 driver stack for ROCm or any Vulkan-capable Radeon driver for Vulkan)
LM Studio (Windows x64 or ARM; AVX2 required; 16 GB RAM recommended; at least 4 GB dedicated VRAM recommended)
llama.cpp prebuilt release zips (CUDA, Vulkan, HIP, SYCL variants exist; SYCL zips named llama-bNNNN-bin-win-sycl-x64.zip)
limits: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 on Windows: AMD's blog says Variable Graphics Memory gives up to 96 GB on a 128 GB machine, with Vulkan llama.cpp (Adrenalin 25.8.1 and later), enabling up to 128B-parameter models. So the Windows GPU cap on Strix Halo is 96 GB of 128 GB per AMD, set via VGM.
Intel SYCL doc: model needs shared memory of at least 8.0 GB for an iGPU and 4.0 GB for a discrete GPU for llama-2-7b Q4_0 (docs example).
Windows 11 22H2 is the validated Windows for HIP SDK 7.2.0; ROCm compat matrix page lists Windows 11 25H2 with Adrenalin 26.10.41.05.
pitfalls: RX 6000 series (6800 XT, 6900 XT etc) and Radeon PRO W6800/W6600: AMD HIP SDK 7.2.0 Windows table shows Runtime, HIP SDK and Debugger all NOT supported for gfx1030/1031/1032. Use Vulkan instead.

NVIDIA datacenter doc (R580 release notes) says graphics APIs on Windows (OpenGL, Vulkan, DX11/12) or any WDDM 2.0+ functionality on Data Center GPUs requires vGPU. Practical consequence for Tesla P40/P100/V100 on Windows: Vulkan and display via WDDM are not supported on them by NVIDIA; use CUDA (TCC mode) only. Whether a specific P40 can be flipped to WDDM is NOT confirmed from a primary page (see not_found).
Forum excerpts (excerpt only, not primary): mixed TCC and WDDM GPUs break WSL2/Docker GPU visibility; one poster says it works when the WDDM card gets the lower driver index. Treat as anecdotal.
Tesla cards have no display output: you need a second GPU or iGPU for the monitor.
Windows Vulkan on Strix Halo: a LM Studio bug report (issue 1048, Oct 2025, excerpt only) described Vulkan runtime not using the GPU on gfx1151 in one version; driver and runtime versions matter.
WSL2 GPU passthrough: not verified from a primary page in this run. NVIDIA CUDA-on-WSL is widely used, but I did not read NVIDIA's doc.

os.summary: Linux has the widest hardware reach. NVIDIA: CUDA 13.x toolkit has dropped Maxwell, Pascal and Volta, but NVIDIA's R580 datacenter driver notes still list CUDA 13.x for Maxwell, Pascal, Volta, so Pascal/Volta stay usable on the R580 driver branch (and with older CUDA 12.x toolkits). AMD: ROCm officially covers RDNA3/RDNA4 plus Radeon PRO V-series (gfx1030) per AMD's matrix; Ollama lists RX 6800 XT/6900 XT and V620 as supported on Linux; MI50/MI60 (gfx906) were put in maintenance mode in ROCm 6.0 and removed in ROCm 7.0 per release notes (excerpt). Vulkan is the fallback for anything else. Intel Arc: llama.cpp SYCL verified on Arc A770/A750/B580 on Linux.
tools: llama.cpp built from source or release binaries (CUDA/HIP/Vulkan/SYCL)
LM Studio AppImage (Ubuntu 20.04+ stated; newer than 22 not well tested; x64 and ARM64)
vLLM (Linux-focused; not verified from a primary page in this run)
limits: Ollama NVIDIA: compute capability 5.0+ and driver 550+; CC 5.0 to 6.2 (Maxwell/Pascal) requires driver 570+.
MLX CUDA on Linux needs NVIDIA SM 7.5 or newer (Turing and up), driver 550.54.14+, CUDA toolkit 12.0+; CUDA 13 package needs driver 580+. Pascal/Volta cannot use MLX-CUDA.
Vulkan under Ollama: needs cap_perfmon (setcap) or root to expose free VRAM; otherwise it estimates sizes.
pitfalls: CUDA Toolkit 13.5 release notes (read): 'Removed support for Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPUs, corresponding to compute capabilities earlier than Turing' and cusolver 'Dropped support for pre-Turing architectures'. So new CUDA toolkits will not target P40/P100/V100/1080 Ti; use pre-built llama.cpp/Ollama binaries that ship their own older CUDA runtimes, or a CUDA 12.x build.

NVIDIA datacenter notes (read): Release 470 was the last driver branch for Kepler. R580 notes still list Maxwell, Pascal, Volta. An NVIDIA Omniverse doc excerpt says Maxwell/Pascal/Volta are not supported by newer branches (excerpt only, search snippet cut off). Exact end-of-life branch statement was not read on an NVIDIA primary page.

AMD MI50/MI60 (gfx906): ROCm 6.0 changelog excerpt says gfx906 'enters maintenance mode in ROCm 6.0'; ROCm 7.0.0 release notes excerpt says 'Removed support for AMD Instinct MI50 and MI60'. Ollama's current Linux list has no gfx906 (lists MI100/gfx908 and up). Expect to pin an old ROCm or use Vulkan; not verified in this run.
Ollama notes you can try HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION (e.g. 10.3.0 for gfx1030-like cards) to force unsupported RDNA2 cards; unofficial.
Ollama on AMD Linux may need the ollama user in the render group; Vulkan on Intel/AMD needs Mesa or vendor packages.
SYCL: the llama.cpp release packages require the same oneAPI and Intel GPU driver versions as the build machine.

os.summary: Apple silicon is a first-class llama.cpp target (Metal, Accelerate, ARM NEON). Ollama uses Metal. LM Studio needs Apple silicon and macOS 14+, and says Intel Macs are not supported. MLX is Apple-silicon macOS 14+ only (it also has a Linux CUDA build, but not a Mac one for NVIDIA). No CUDA on macOS. Apple's own eGPU page says eGPUs need a Mac with an Intel processor, so NO eGPU on Apple silicon. Memory is unified, so RAM size is the model-size budget; the GPU can use roughly 75% by default on high-memory Macs.
tools: LM Studio (Apple silicon, macOS 14.0+, 16 GB+ recommended, 8 GB possible with small models and small context)
limits: Default GPU wired-memory limit is about 75% of RAM on higher-memory Macs (blog excerpts; tweakable with sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb; value 0 returns to default). Apple did not publish this in anything I read.

Sizing rule of thumb for the site (derived from the 75% figure, NOT measured, not from a primary page): 16 GB gives about 12 GB for the GPU, 32 GB about 24 GB, 64 GB about 48 GB, 128 GB about 96 GB by default. Smaller-RAM Macs reportedly get a lower share (excerpt said ~75% 'on higher-memory machines'); raising the limit can reach higher values.

Intel Macs: Apple says eGPUs work on Intel Macs with Thunderbolt 3 running macOS High Sierra 10.13.4 or later. LM Studio does not support Intel Macs. Intel+eGPU for LLMs is therefore limited to Ollama/llama.cpp builds; not tested or verified here.
pitfalls: No eGPU on Apple silicon (confirmed: Apple page 102363 says an eGPU requires a Mac with an Intel processor).

sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb resets on reboot unless persisted via a LaunchDaemon (shown in a Medium excerpt) or /etc/sysctl.conf (one blog says SIP may need disabling for sysctl.conf; unverified). Setting the limit too high can starve macOS and freeze the machine (blog guidance, not Apple).

Price per GB of usable memory is Apple's selling point against PC GPUs; Mac prices used: Mac mini M6 32 GB $1,299; M5 Pro 64 GB $2,699; Studio M5 Max 128 GB about $5,100 (supplied by Ian, not re-verified here). Mac memory bandwidth is lower than discrete GPUs, so tokens per second are lower; no benchmark was run in this research.

cross_os_tools.note: Backends: CUDA, HIP, Vulkan, SYCL, Metal, OpenVINO (in progress), CPU/BLAS, RPC (README backend table, read). Format: GGUF.
CUDA, ROCm v7, Vulkan (Windows/Linux), Metal (Apple). Docs read.
macOS: Apple silicon only, macOS 14+; Windows x64/ARM with AVX2; Linux AppImage x64/ARM64. Intel Macs not supported.
Apple silicon + macOS >= 14.0; MLX also exists for Linux CUDA, but is mainly a macOS tool. Windows not found in the install doc extract.
No vLLM primary page read in this run; do not publish OS claims without reading its docs.

mac_memory.default_gpu_share: About 75% of unified memory on higher-memory Apple silicon Macs (from third-party blog excerpts; 0 means 'use default'). Implies roughly 96 GB usable on a 128 GB machine, 48 GB on 64 GB. Smaller-RAM Macs may get a smaller share; not verified. Apple has no page I read that states this.
mac_memory.how_to_raise: sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=<MB> (e.g. 57344 for ~56 GB on a 64 GB Mac per Reddit excerpt; 61440 for 60 GB per Medium excerpt). Resets on reboot; persist with a LaunchDaemon that runs sysctl at load (Medium excerpt) or /etc/sysctl.conf (one blog says SIP may block it; unverified). Leave several GB for macOS. Set to 0 to restore default.
